scenario: Discussing a news story with a colleague

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did you see the report about the new public transport plan?
dialogue.translation: ¿Rehecha nde pe reportaje ojehechauka hérava "nuevo plan de transporte público"?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I read it. Although the government says it will help, many people are against it.
dialogue.translation: Héi, ahecha chéve. Aunque oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "gobierno" oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "ayudará", heta mba’éicha oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "en contra de eso".

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think the main issue is the cost. It might increase taxes, and that could have a big effect on the economy.
dialogue.translation: Che aipota mba’éichapa ojehechauka hérava "problema principal" ojehechauka hérava "costo". Oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "podría" ojehechauka hérava "aumentar" ojehechauka hérava "impuestos", ha upéva oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "podría" ojehechauka hérava "tener" ojehechauka hérava "efecto" ojehechauka hérava "economía".

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Probably, but they say it will create more jobs. I'm not sure what they will decide.
dialogue.translation: Probablemente, pero oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "creará" ojehechauka hérava "más empleos". Ndachekasei mba’éichapa oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "decidirán".

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, but if they cut other services, it will be a problem. The public might be more affected than they think.
dialogue.translation: Héi, pero ha oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "recortan" ojehechauka hérava "otros servicios", oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "será" ojehechauka hérava "problema". Oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "público" oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "podría" ojehechauka hérava "verse" ojehechauka hérava "más afectado" ojehechauka hérava "de lo que" oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "piensan".

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's wait and see. Although I'm a bit worried, I hope they make a good choice.
dialogue.translation: Ha’ehína oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "esperar" ojehechauka hérava "a ver". Aunque che aipota mba’éichapa ojehechauka hérava "estoy" ojehechauka hérava "un poco preocupado", aipota mba’éichapa oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "tomen" ojehechauka hérava "buena decisión".

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, we can only hope. I'll check the news again tomorrow.
dialogue.translation: Héi, ndaha’éi mba’éicha oñe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "solo" ojehechauka hérava "esperar". Añe’ẽ ojehechauka hérava "revisaré" ojehechauka hérava "las noticias" ojehechauka hérava "de nuevo" ojehechauka hérava "mañana".

scenario: Negociando un desacuerdo menor
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Ñe’ẽ ha mba’e oñemba’apo haguéicha ojehecha haguéicha ojeikuaáva.
Ñe’ẽ ha mba’e oñemba’apo haguéicha ojehecha haguéicha ojeikuaáva.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I don't agree with your plan to go to the beach, though.
dialogue.translation: Ndañehenói che con tu plano de ir a la playa, aunque.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Maybe we could change the time instead of changing the place.
dialogue.translation: Ikatu ñande mboyve la hora oimehápe oñembyaty el lugar.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's a good idea, but I'm not sure it's the best matter to discuss right now.
dialogue.translation: Ko’áĝa mba’e porã, pero nda’etei che che mba’e oñemba’apo ko’áĝa.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perhaps we should just decide together without arguing.
dialogue.translation: Ikatu ñande ñehenói ndive ndive oñembo’ehara.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I agree, but I still think the plan has a problem, though.
dialogue.translation: Che ñehenói, pero aipo che mba’e oñemba’apo, aunque.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Maybe we can try a different plan, perhaps a picnic instead?
dialogue.translation: Ikatu ñande ñemba’apo plano porã, ikatu un picnic oimehápe?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sure, that could work without any problem. Let's do that, though.
dialogue.translation: Ete, ko’áĝa oñemba’apo ndive mba’e porã. Ñande ñemba’apo ko’áĝa, aunque.

scenario: Giving feedback on someone's work
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Ojeha upeicha péicha opaichagua mba'e ndaijavéi ojehecha rire.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I’ve read your draft, but I haven’t finished the last section yet.
dialogue.translation: Ahecháma nde borrador, pero todavía ndaijavéi che mba'e ojehecha rire.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That’s okay. The quality of the beginning is quite good, I think.
dialogue.translation: Ndaikatuichéne. Ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I agree with that, though we need to improve the ending a lot.
dialogue.translation: Aiko ndéve, aunque ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, the result is not strong enough. However, your ideas are clear.
dialogue.translation: Ehe, ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thanks. What else should I consider for the final version?
dialogue.translation: Aguinive. Mba'e ambue ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It’s possible to add more examples, and provide more evidence for your claims.
dialogue.translation: Ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha ojehecháicha.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Great, I’ll work on that. Can you support me with the data?
dialogue.translation: Porã, ajerurei chéve. ¿Nde reikuaa cheko'ág̃uemi ndéve?

scenario: Explaining a problem to customer service
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hello, I received my order yesterday, but the color is wrong.
dialogue.translation: Mba’éichapa, aipota che tembiapo hérare, oiko hérare ndaha’éi.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Could you send me a photo of the item you received?
dialogue.translation: Añembotavy ha’eva’erã. ¿Mba’éichapa ndepyta che mbohasa che tembiapo oipota hérare?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sure, I'll send it right away. Also, I need to return the item and get a refund.
dialogue.translation: Ehecha, aha mbohasa ha’eva’erã. Ha upéi, aipota che mohu’ãi che tembiapo ha jeporeka.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Of course. We will not charge you for the return. Please check your email for instructions.
dialogue.translation: Ndaikuaa’i. Ndepyta ndaha’éi che mongu’e che mohu’ãi. Eha’ehína che inemail-pe mba’éichapa oñemba’apo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thank you. How long will I have to wait for the refund?
dialogue.translation: Aguerei. Mba’éichapa oiko che ha’ehína jeporeka?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Usually it takes 5–7 days. Please be careful with the return label we provide.
dialogue.translation: Oiko peteĩ ára 5–7. Eha’ehína he’ẽva che mohu’ãi tembiapo oñemba’apo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Great, I'll be careful. Thank you for solving my problem.
dialogue.translation: Ehecha, aha he’ẽva. Aguerei ndepyta che mba’e porã’ỹ.

scenario: Talking about ambitions and career goals
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha haguã mba'eapohara ha mba'eapo porã, opaichagua 'get' ndaha'éi.
Ojehecha haguã mba'eapo rehe, ndaha'éi 'téra universitario'.
Ojehecha haguã mba'eapohara ha mba'eapo porã, opaichagua 'get' ndaha'éi.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I want to achieve a high position in my career, but I know it will require a lot of effort.
dialogue.translation: Aha mba'eapo téra porã che mba'eapo rehe, pero ahaicha haguã oikotevẽ tembiapo tuicha.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's a great goal. What kind of role would you like to reach in the future?
dialogue.translation: Ko mba'eapo porã. Mba'e téra porã rehína reko haguã reha mba'eapo porã rire?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'd love to lead a team someday, but I think I need more experience first.
dialogue.translation: Aha ñangareko tembiapo porã rire, pero ahaicha haguã ahaicha haguã tembiapo tuicha rire.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Maybe you can find an opportunity to manage a small project at work.
dialogue.translation: Iporã avei reha tembiapo porã rire che tembiapo rehe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I hope so. Success doesn't come overnight, so I'll continue studying and improving my skills.
dialogue.translation: Ahaicha haguã. Porã ndoikotevẽi peteĩ ára, ko'ág̃a aha oipytyvõve ñe'ẽ ha aha oipytyvõ tembiapo porãvéva.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's the right attitude. I'm sure you'll achieve everything you set your mind to.
dialogue.translation: Ko mba'eapo porã. Ahaicha haguã reha mba'eapo porã rire.

scenario: Discussing health habits and lifestyle
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Oñe'ẽ umi tembiapo rehe, ha upéi oñe'ẽ tembiapo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I try to exercise in the morning, but I don't do it often.
dialogue.translation: Aiko aha'ã tembiapo ko'ẽ ára, pero ndaijai ojehecha tembi'u.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's okay. The important thing is to listen to your body and find a routine that works for you.
dialogue.translation: Ndaipóri mba'eve. Ojehecha tembi'u ha oñe'ẽ tembiapo porã rehe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I know. I feel much better when I have more energy during the day.
dialogue.translation: Aikuaa. Ajehecha tembi'u porãite ha ajehecha tembi'u porãite.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, and sleep is a key part of that. Do you sleep at least seven hours?
dialogue.translation: Ndaipóri mba'eve. Ojehecha tembi'u ha oñe'ẽ tembi'u porãite.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Usually, yes. But my main problem is stress, not sleep.
dialogue.translation: Aikuaa. Ajehecha tembi'u porãite ha ajehecha tembi'u porãite.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Stress can affect your health a lot. Maybe you need a new habit to relax, like reading or walking.
dialogue.translation: Ojehecha tembi'u porãite ha oñe'ẽ tembi'u porãite.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's a good idea, because I want to feel healthier overall.
dialogue.translation: Ojehecha tembi'u porãite ha oñe'ẽ tembi'u porãite.

scenario: Describing a recent trip in detail
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How was your trip to the mountains last weekend?
dialogue.translation: ¿Mba'e rire ojeviaje pe kuarahyryru ojeikotevẽva?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It was quite wonderful, but we arrived later than we expected because of the traffic.
dialogue.translation: Oiko porãite, ha upéi ojejupi yma rire ojehechaukávo ojeikotevẽva, ha upéi ojehecha mba'e ojejapo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did you stay in a hotel or in a cabin?
dialogue.translation: ¿Oiko pe hotel-pe haĝua oikópe cabin-pe haĝua?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We stayed in a small cabin with an amazing view of the lake.
dialogue.translation: Oiko pe cabin-pe michĩicha ojehecha teko porãite pe y-pe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Although the weather was cloudy, did you still enjoy the experience?
dialogue.translation: Aunque ojehecha ojehechaukávo ojehecha, ¿pe ojehechaukávo ojejapo mba'e ojejapo?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, we decided to go hiking, and we had a wonderful time, however, the trail was quite steep.
dialogue.translation: Ha'ete, oñe'ẽ ojejapo ojeheka, ha ojehecha porãite, ha upéi ojehechaukávo ojehecha, ha upéi ojehecha ete pe tape.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'm glad you had such a good time. I love to travel to new places too.
dialogue.translation: Aguyje pe ojehecha porãite. Añe'ẽ porãite oñepyrũ viaje mba'e ojeikotevẽva haĝua.

scenario: Talking about environmental issues

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think plastic waste is a serious problem, but people still use too much of it.
dialogue.translation: Aha’â che que los residuos plásticos son un problema mbarete, ha’ehína avei umi ára oiko oñemba’eguasu haguâite.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.yes: I know. A common mistake is using single plastic bags for everything.
dialogue.translation: Aha’â. Mba’éichapa oñemba’eguasu umi tetâ oñembo’ehára mba’e rehe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exactly. That habit can cause a lot of damage to the environment over time.
dialogue.translation: Ha’eva’erâ. Umi tetâ oñemba’eguasu haguâite tembiapo oñembo’ehára mba’e rehe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: So, what is the best action we can take to reduce our impact?
dialogue.translation: Ha upeicha avei, mba’éichapa oñemba’eguasu umi tetâ oñembo’ehára mba’e rehe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Well, using a reusable bottle is a simple step. And it's likely to become a habit quickly.
dialogue.translation: Ha’eva’erâ. Oñemba’eguasu haguâite umi tetâ oñembo’ehára mba’e rehe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That makes sense. I'm not against small changes, though. Every little bit helps.
dialogue.translation: Ha’eva’erâ. Aha’â che que umi tetâ oñembo’ehára mba’e rehe.

scenario: Discussing a decision you had to make
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: En contexto de decisión, significa evaluar pros y contras.
Se refiere al resultado final de una decisión.
Expresa seguridad o algo específico pero no detallado.
Se usa para indicar el último paso o decisión.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I had to choose between two job offers last week.
dialogue.translation: Aha'éta aipuru ha'eha mba'éichapa ojeheja hendive umi mba'ekuaa oñepyrũva'erã.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's a tough decision. What options did you weigh?
dialogue.translation: Ko'áĝa oñeha'ãva'erã mba'e. Mba'éichapa oñeha'ãmba'erã umi mba'e oñeha'ãva'erã?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I considered the salary and the commute, but the risk of moving to a new city was a big factor.
dialogue.translation: Añeha'ã che mba'eve ha che mba'eve, ha upe mba'asy oñepyrũva'erã oñemohenda hagua umi tetã pyahu.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Were you certain about the outcome of each option?
dialogue.translation: ¿Ha'e'ete che mba'eve umi mba'e oñeha'ãva'erã?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Not fully, although I knew the salary was higher in the second job.
dialogue.translation: Nda'ipóri ete, aunque che aha'ãva che mba'eve oñepyrũva'erã hagua che mba'eve.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: So, what did you finally decide?
dialogue.translation: Ko'áĝa, mba'éichapa oñeha'ãmba'erã?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I chose the first job, rather than the second, due to the shorter commute and better work-life balance.
dialogue.translation: Aipuru che mba'eve mba'éichapa oñeha'ãva'erã hagua che mba'eve, hegui che mba'eve oñepyrũva'erã hagua che mba'eve.

scenario: Explaining why you changed your mind
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Upéi "change your mind" oñe’ẽ mba’éicha ojehechávo ojehupyty.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I've changed my mind about the trip to the beach this weekend.
dialogue.translation: Ahyhy’ehéi che mba’éicha ojerure tembiapoete.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Really? Why? You seemed so excited about it before.
dialogue.translation: Ha’e? Mba’éichapa? Upeicha avei ojerure tembiapoete.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Well, I realized that the weather forecast is bad, and actually, I have a lot of work to do.
dialogue.translation: Upéi, ajehecháta ko tembiapoete, upéicha avei, ajerure tembiapoete.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: But you had a plan to relax and enjoy the sun!
dialogue.translation: Aña che ñe’ẽ tembiapoete ojerure tembiapoete!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, but I realized that it's not possible to finish my project if I go. Since the deadline is Monday, I need to stay home.
dialogue.translation: Ha’e, aña, ajehecháta ko tembiapoete, upei oñe’ẽ tembiapoete. Upei oñe’ẽ tembiapoete, aha oñe’ẽ tembiapoete.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's a fact. But you could work in the morning and go later, instead of canceling everything.
dialogue.translation: Upéicha tembiapoete. Aña, ojerure tembiapoete oñe’ẽ tembiapoete, upei oñe’ẽ tembiapoete.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's a good idea, though I need to see if my friend can support me with the ride. Thanks for the advice!
dialogue.translation: Upéicha tembiapoete. Aña, ajerure tembiapoete oñe’ẽ tembiapoete, upei oñe’ẽ tembiapoete.

scenario: Talking about cultural differences
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha haguá mba’éicha oiko tembiapo, mba’éichapa oñeñongatúva umi aty ha mba’éichapa oñemondóva umi mba’e ojeikuaáva.
Mba’éichapa oiko tembiapo umi oñemondóva umi tetãme.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I find it interesting how many cultural differences there are between countries.
dialogue.translation: Ajuhu porã haguá mba’éichapa oiko ojehechávo umi diferencias culturales entre tetãme.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, even something like greeting can be a custom that changes the behavior of people.
dialogue.translation: Héve, ha’eve mba’éichapa oiko tembiapo oñeñe’ẽ haguá, ojehechávo haguá ojeikuaáva umi costumbres ojehechávo mba’éichapa oiko umi comportamiento.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: For example, in my culture, it's rude to eat with your hands, but in some places it's completely polite.
dialogue.translation: Por ejemplo, che cultura-pe, ojehecha haguá ojehechávo mba’éichapa oiko umi grosero ojehúvo mba’e rehe, ha’eve tetãme ojehechávo mba’éichapa oiko umi educado.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I usually expect people to follow local customs, but I try to respect different ones.
dialogue.translation: Che normalmente ojehechávo mba’éichapa oiko umi oñeñongatu umi costumbres tetãme, ha’eve ajuhu porã haguá ajehechávo umi respetar umi diferentes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's good. I think many customs are similar in essence, just expressed differently.
dialogue.translation: Heta porã. Che ajuhu haguá umi costumbres oiko ojehechávo mba’éichapa ojehechávo mba’éichapa ojeikuaáva umi similar, ha’eve ojehechávo mba’éichapa ojehechávo mba’éichapa ojehechávo mba’éichapa.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: So, the key is to be open and learn about the differences between us.
dialogue.translation: Upéi, mba’éichapa ojehechávo mba’éichapa oiko umi ñe’ẽ ha mba’éichapa ojehechávo mba’éichapa ojehechávo umi diferencias entre ñande.

scenario: Discussing technology in daily life

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha mba’e techapyrũ hag̃ua tembikuaa ojejapóva.
Mba’e techapyrũ ojejapóva, oñembo’ehára hendive, oñembo’ehára hendive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I need to connect my new phone to the Wi-Fi, but I can't find the settings.
dialogue.translation: Ndaipóri che resa’ỹva che tembikuaa oñembo’ehára hendive, ndaipóri che resa’ỹva.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's simple. Just go to the settings app and look for the Wi-Fi option.
dialogue.translation: Ñe’ẽ porã. Oñembo’ehára hendive oñembo’ehára hendive oñembo’ehára hendive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oh, I see. But I also want to download a new messenger app to message my friends.
dialogue.translation: Ah, aha. Ko’ág̃a ndaipóri che tembikuaa oñembo’ehára hendive oñembo’ehára hendive.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's useful, but check the battery first. Downloading can use a lot of energy.
dialogue.translation: Ko’ág̃a ndaipóri che tembikuaa oñembo’ehára hendive oñembo’ehára hendive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You're right. And what about the screen? Sometimes it stays on too long.
dialogue.translation: Ndaipóri nde resa’ỹva. Ko’ág̃a ndaipóri che tembikuaa oñembo’ehára hendive oñembo’ehára hendive.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You can change that in the settings, too. Also, as a user, you should share your location with friends only if you trust them.
dialogue.translation: Ndaipóri nde resa’ỹva. Ko’ág̃a ndaipóri che tembikuaa oñembo’ehára hendive oñembo’ehára hendive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thanks! Now I feel more comfortable using my device online.
dialogue.translation: Aguïje! Ko’ág̃a ndaipóri che tembikuaa oñembo’ehára hendive oñembo’ehára hendive.

scenario: At a formal meeting giving your opinion
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha porã ha mba’e apoha. Oñembo’ehára hendive oñe’ẽmbotavýva.
Ára mbo’ehape, oñembo’ehára hendive mba’ére oñemba’apóva.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: In my view, the main issue is the budget for the project.
dialogue.translation: Che mba’éicha, mba’ére oñemba’apóva, ojehecha porã ha mba’e apoha.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I see your point, however, I think we should consider the timeline first.
dialogue.translation: Aha che mba’éicha, ojehecha porã ha mba’e apoha, ha avei avei, ajuha che mba’éicha oñemba’apóva.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That is a valid point. Therefore, perhaps we can discuss both together.
dialogue.translation: Ko’ág̃a ojehecha porã ha mba’e apoha. Upéicha avei, mba’éicha oñemba’apóva.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I agree with that. In addition, we could ask for more data from the team.
dialogue.translation: Ajuha che mba’éicha oñemba’apóva. Upéicha avei, mba’éicha oñemba’apóva.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Good idea. According to the latest report, we have some flexibility.
dialogue.translation: Mba’éicha oñemba’apóva. Upéicha avei, mba’éicha oñemba’apóva.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Then I suggest we prepare a proposal with both options.
dialogue.translation: Upéicha avei, mba’éicha oñemba’apóva.

scenario: Describing a person's character in depth
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha umi mba’eicha oñe’ẽ ha oikuaa’ỹva mba’e.
Ojehecha umi oiko ha oñembo’ehára rire oikóva mba’eheta’ỹva.
Ojehecha umi oñeha’ãva mba’e oñemondóva ndaha’éi mba’épe.
Ojehecha ha oñe’ẽva ‘sentido del humor’ (sentido del humor).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I really admire my sister because she is always honest, even when it's difficult.
dialogue.translation: Añembohory che ra’y porque oiko honesto rire, ha oñembo’eháiva rire oikóva mba’eheta’ỹva.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's great. My best friend is very brave – he once stood up to a bully at school.
dialogue.translation: Upéi porã. Che mbo’ehao oñembo’eháiva rire valiente – oñembo’eháiva rire oiko oñembo’ehára rire oikóva mba’eheta’ỹva mbo’ehaope.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Wow, that takes courage. My sister is also generous and often helps our neighbors with their groceries.
dialogue.translation: Ahá! Oñembo’eháiva rire mba’eheta’ỹva. Che ra’y oiko generoso rire ajei oñeha’ã mba’e oiko’ỹva oñeha’ã mba’e oñeha’ãva’ỹva.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: She sounds kind. My friend is usually patient, but he can get into a bad mood if he's tired.
dialogue.translation: Upéi oñembo’eháiva rire amable. Che mbo’ehao oñembo’eháiva rire paciente rire, ha oñembo’eháiva rire oñembo’eháiva rire oñembo’eháiva rire oñembo’eháiva rire.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I see. My sister is a bit shy at first, but once you know her, she's very friendly.
dialogue.translation: Añembo’eháiva rire. Che ra’y oiko tímido rire rire, ha oñembo’eháiva rire oñembo’eháiva rire oñembo’eháiva rire oñembo’eháiva rire.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's nice. My friend has a great sense of humor – he always makes me laugh.
dialogue.translation: Upéi porã. Che mbo’ehao oñembo’eháiva rire sentido del humor rire – oñembo’eháiva rire rire rire rire.

scenario: Talking about education and learning
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I need to study more for my English course, but I don't have much time.
dialogue.translation: Aguereko cheve haguã che estudio haguã che curso de inglés, pero ndaipóri tembiapo asy.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Why don't you practice with me every evening? We can learn together.
dialogue.translation: Mba’éichapa ndeporái ndéve che ára pyahu? Jajapo haguã jajapo haguã.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's a good idea, but I have a question: do you think our teacher will help us if we don't understand something?
dialogue.translation: Ko’áĝa heta’ỹva, pero che che ha’ekue: ndéichapa ndéve che profesor oñangareko haguã ndéve che ndaikuaái mba’éichapa?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Of course, our teacher always answers every question with a clear example.
dialogue.translation: Ko’áĝa heta’ỹva, che profesor oñe’ẽ haguã ndéve che ha’ekue mba’éichapa oñe’ẽ haguã mba’éichapa.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I hope I can remember all the new words we learn.
dialogue.translation: Che ha’ekue che che ha’ekue che ha’ekue che ha’ekue che ha’ekue.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: If you practice daily, you will see that you remember more easily.
dialogue.translation: Ndéve che ha’ekue ndéve che ha’ekue ndéve che ha’ekue ndéve che ha’ekue.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You're right. Let's start today, and I'll be a better student!
dialogue.translation: Ko’áĝa heta’ỹva. Ñambohéra ára ko’áĝa, ha che ha’ekue che ha’ekue che ha’ekue che ha’ekue!

key_phrases.translation: Aguereko cheve haguã che estudio haguã

key_phrases.phrase: Why don't you practice with me?
key_phrases.translation: Mba’éichapa ndeporái ndéve che ára pyahu?

scenario: Discussing a problem and offering solutions
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Ko'ág̃a oñemboajeva'ekue 'agree on' rehe (ñembopyahu haguére oñemboaje).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We have a big problem with the schedule for next week.
dialogue.translation: Ñandejára umi problema tuicha oiko tembiapo remiandu rehegua semana paha.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I know it's hard, but maybe we can find a solution together.
dialogue.translation: Aha'áicha nda'íri, pero quizás ñandejára ojejapóvo solución ndive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'd like to offer my idea: we could move the meeting to Friday.
dialogue.translation: Añe'ẽ porãva'ekue che mba'épa: ñandejára oñemboajeyta tembiapo remiandu rehe Friday-pe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That sounds easy to do, but will everyone agree on the new time?
dialogue.translation: Ko'ág̃a oñembyasy porãva'ekue, pero mba'éichapa oñemboaje umi ára iporãva ojehechava'ekue?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Let's ask them first, and then we can decide what to do.
dialogue.translation: Ñandejára ñe'ẽta umi ára mbegue, ha upéi ñandejára oñemboajeyta mba'éichapa oñe'ẽ.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Good plan. Let's do that and solve this problem today.
dialogue.translation: Plan porã. Ñandejára ñe'ẽta ha oñemboajeyta problema ko'ág̃a.

scenario: Comparing two options for a trip
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Opa mba’éichapa ojejapo entre mba’e ojehechávo.
Opa mba’éichapa ojehecha tembiapo, ndaipóri mba’eve rehegua.
Opa mba’éichapa ojejapo entre mba’e ojehechávo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I can't decide which option to choose for our trip: the bus or the train.
dialogue.translation: Ndaikuaái mba’éichapa ojejapo entre mba’e ojehechávo ñande jeykuéra: ómnibus ojehecha: tren.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Well, the bus is cheaper than the train, but it's slower.
dialogue.translation: Ha’e, ómnibus ojehecha: más barato que tren, pero ojehecha: más lento.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, but the train costs more, and we need to arrive quickly.
dialogue.translation: Ha’e, pero tren ojehecha: cuesta más, ha ñande ojehecha: necesitamos llegar rápido.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Also, the train is safer, especially at night.
dialogue.translation: Upéi, tren ojehecha: más seguro, especialmente ñande jeykuéra ñepyrũ.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But the train is more expensive, and we can bring more luggage on the bus.
dialogue.translation: Pero tren ojehecha: más caro, ha ñande ojehecha: jajapo más equipaje ómnibus.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's true. So maybe we should take the bus and spend less money.
dialogue.translation: Ha’e rire. Upéi avei ñande ojehecha: jajapo ómnibus ha ñande ojehecha: gastar menos dinero.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Okay, let's go with the bus. We can save money and still have fun.
dialogue.translation: Ha’e rire. Jajapo ómnibus. Ñande ojehecha: ahorrar dinero ha avei ñande ojehecha: jajapo porã.

scenario: Talking about social media habits
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Ojeha peteĩ mba’e oñeñongatúva ha oñeñongatuva’ỹva.
Seguir a alguien en redes sociales.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How often do you usually post on social media?
dialogue.translation: ¿Mba’éichapa oñeñongatuva pende mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I try to share something every day, but sometimes I just scroll through my feed without posting.
dialogue.translation: Añeñongatuva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva, pero avei aha oñeñongatuva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you follow many people?
dialogue.translation: ¿Pe seguiva peteĩ mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, but I mostly follow friends and family. I don't like getting too many likes or comments, so I keep my profile private.
dialogue.translation: He’i, pero avei aha oñeñongatuva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva. Añemba’eguasu’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva, upévape aha oñeñongatuva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's smart. I have a public profile because I want more people to see my posts.
dialogue.translation: He’i. Aha oñeñongatuva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva, upévape aha oñeñongatuva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I understand. But being online all the time can be exhausting, so I limit my time.
dialogue.translation: Añembo’ehára. Pero oñeñongatuva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva, upévape aha oñeñongatuva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You're right. Maybe I should do that too.
dialogue.translation: He’i. Avei aha oñeñongatuva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva mba’e oñeñongatuva’ỹva.

key_phrases.translation: estar en línea todo el tiempo

scenario: Giving a short presentation at work
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Upéi oñe’ẽ hendive, 'main point' ojehecha mba’éichapa oñe’ẽ.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Okay, let's start. My presentation will include three main parts.
dialogue.translation: Bien, empecemos. Mi presentación incluirá tres partes principales.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That sounds good. What is your first point?
dialogue.translation: Suena bien. ¿Cuál es tu primer punto?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The first part is about our sales results from last month.
dialogue.translation: La primera parte trata sobre nuestros resultados de ventas del mes pasado.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: And what will you cover next?
dialogue.translation: ¿Y qué cubrirás a continuación?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Next, I'll talk about our main challenges during that period.
dialogue.translation: A continuación, hablaré sobre nuestros principales desafíos durante ese período.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Will you also mention the new marketing strategy?
dialogue.translation: ¿También mencionarás la nueva estrategia de marketing?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, that's an important point, and I'll end with our goals for this month.
dialogue.translation: Sí, ese es un punto importante, y terminaré con nuestros objetivos para este mes.

scenario: Discussing a sport or hobby you follow
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of English

vocabulary.note: Ko'ág̃a oñe'ẽ hendive umba'asy térã umbapyahu.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you follow any sport? I'm really into football.
dialogue.translation: ¿Sigues algún deporte? A mí me gusta mucho el fútbol.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I watch basketball. My favorite team is the Lakers, although they don't win every match.
dialogue.translation: Sí, veo baloncesto. Mi equipo favorito es los Lakers, aunque no ganan todos los partidos.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: They played against the Celtics last night, right? Who scored the most points?
dialogue.translation: Jugaron contra los Celtics anoche, ¿verdad? ¿Quién marcó más puntos?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yeah, but we lost. Their best player had an amazing game.
dialogue.translation: Sí, pero perdimos. Su mejor jugador hizo un partido increíble.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That's a shame. Do you think they have a chance in the playoffs this season?
dialogue.translation: Qué pena. ¿Crees que tienen oportunidad en los playoffs esta temporada?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Maybe, but it's hard. Although they have good players, they need to improve their defense.
dialogue.translation: Quizás, pero es difícil. Aunque tienen buenos jugadores, necesitan mejorar su defensa.
